refuter.evidence: §1985:III.2 defines 'A variable occurrence data item is a table element which is repeated a variable number of times. Such an item must contain an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause in its data description entry, or be subordinate to such an item.' (cite.py: OK §1985:III.2 the text is in the clause). SR1b (cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR1b) forbids OCCURS on an entry that 'Has a variable occurrence data item subordinate to it.' The reader's own requirement says the same ('an ODO table element or an item under one'). Probe refute-1985-05/c5/g1.cob: 05 T OCCURS 1 TO 3 DEPENDING ON N. 10 U OCCURS 2 TIMES. 15 V PIC X. V is subordinate to the ODO entry T, so V is a variable occurrence data item, and U carries an OCCURS with V subordinate to it; --std 85 prints 'R=ABCD V=C' (compiled and ran; --std 2023 the same). The reader's ok.cob escapes the rule only because its inner OCCURS is elementary (no subordinate). g2/g3/g4 (ODO under a fixed OCCURS, at depth, Linkage) are refused COBOL0854, correctly. OdoResolvePass's test is 'an ODO entry below an OCCURS entry'; it never asks whether an OCCURS entry inside an ODO table has subordinates, which the 1985 definition makes variable occurrence items. Counter-reading noted: §1985:VI.5.15.6 GR5 lists 'b. It is a variable occurrence data item' and 'c. It is a data item that is subordinate to a variable occurrence data item' separately, which hints the drafters sometimes used the narrower sense; but III.2 is the edition's definition and SR1b leans on it.
refuter.corrected: NONCONFORMING (under-rejects), cause (c): at 1985 the III.2 definition makes every item subordinate to an ODO entry a variable occurrence data item, so an OCCURS entry inside an ODO table that has any subordinate entry must be refused; the compiler admits it at --std 85 (and at 2023). Repro refute-1985-05/c5/g1.cob.
